defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job do @moduledoc """ A single job workspace: the room-by-room checklist, clock in/out with running earnings, and incident reporting. Route: `/field/jobs/:id`. A cleaner who opens a job not assigned to them is redirected straight back to `/field` with a flash — the page exposes entry codes and client details, so an unassigned cleaner must never see it render at all (reconciled with story 838's criterion 7123 and story 844's criterion 7129). Office staff (an account's `:owner`/`:admin`) can open any job in the account, assigned or not — story 836's criterion 7153 exercises exactly that, completing a job that was never assigned to a specific cleaner. ## Dependencies - `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` - `CleanerCrm.Quality` - `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` - `CleanerCrm.Accounts` — only to distinguish office staff from a field cleaner for the check above. - `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.ChecklistComponent` - `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.IncidentFormComponent` """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view alias CleanerCrm.Accounts alias CleanerCrm.Money alias CleanerCrm.Quality alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, TimeEntry} alias CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.{ChecklistComponent, IncidentFormComponent} @impl true def render(assigns) do ~H"""
<.header> {client_name(@job)} <:subtitle> {@job.scheduled_date} · {format_time(@job.start_time)}–{format_time(@job.end_time)} <:actions> Complete

You're still clocked in to your {@clock_in_warning.client && @clock_in_warning.client.name} job — clock out there first.

Clocked in {format_duration(@elapsed_seconds)} <.button data-test="clock-out-button" phx-click="clock_out">Clock Out

Missing clock-out — remember to clock out when you're done.

Clocked out {format_duration(@last_worked_seconds)} <.button data-test="clock-in-button" phx-click="clock_in">Clock In

{Money.format_cents(@earnings_cents)}

<.live_component module={ChecklistComponent} id="checklist" current_scope={@current_scope} job={@job} checklist={@checklist} /> <.live_component module={IncidentFormComponent} id="incident-form" current_scope={@current_scope} job={@job} />
""" end @impl true def mount(%{"id" => id}, _session, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, id) if assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job) or office_staff?(scope) do {:ok, socket |> assign(:job, job) |> assign(:page_title, "Job") |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) |> load_checklist() |> load_time_state() |> maybe_schedule_tick()} else {:ok, socket |> put_flash(:error, "This job is not assigned to you.") |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")} end end @impl true def handle_event("clock_in", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job case TimeTracking.clock_in(scope, job) do {:ok, _entry} -> {:noreply, socket |> assign(:clock_in_warning, nil) |> load_time_state()} {:error, {:already_clocked_in, other_job}} -> {:noreply, assign(socket, :clock_in_warning, Scheduling.get_job!(scope, other_job.id))} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket} end end def handle_event("clock_out", _params, socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job case TimeTracking.clock_out(scope, job) do {:ok, _entry} -> {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} {:error, _reason} -> {:noreply, socket} end end @impl true def handle_info(:job_completed, socket) do job = Scheduling.get_job!(socket.assigns.current_scope, socket.assigns.job.id) {:noreply, socket |> assign(:job, job) |> load_checklist()} end def handle_info(:checklist_changed, socket), do: {:noreply, load_checklist(socket)} def handle_info(:tick, socket) do if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) {:noreply, load_time_state(socket)} end defp maybe_schedule_tick(socket) do if connected?(socket), do: Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 1000) socket end defp assigned_to_viewer?(scope, job), do: job.cleaner_id == scope.user.id defp office_staff?(%{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin] end defp office_staff?(_scope), do: false # Every job gets a checklist to complete through, even a trivially # empty one for a job nothing ever assigned a template to — lazily # instantiated here so `ChecklistComponent`'s completion flow (and # the invoice it triggers) is the one path every job completes # through, rather than a second one this view would otherwise need # for the no-checklist case. defp load_checklist(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job checklist = case Quality.get_checklist_for_job(scope, job) do nil -> {:ok, checklist} = Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, []) checklist checklist -> checklist end assign(socket, :checklist, checklist) end defp load_time_state(socket) do scope = socket.assigns.current_scope job = socket.assigns.job entries = TimeTracking.list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job) last_resolved = entries |> Enum.filter(&TimeEntry.resolved?/1) |> List.last() socket |> assign(:open_entry, TimeTracking.open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job)) |> assign(:elapsed_seconds, TimeTracking.elapsed_seconds(scope, job)) |> assign(:last_worked_seconds, last_resolved && Earnings.worked_seconds(last_resolved)) |> assign(:earnings_cents, TimeTracking.job_earnings_cents(scope, job)) end defp client_name(%{client: %{name: name}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(%{property: %{client: %{name: name}}}) when is_binary(name), do: name defp client_name(_job), do: "Job" defp format_time(time), do: Calendar.strftime(time, "%-H:%M") defp format_duration(nil), do: "0m" defp format_duration(seconds) do hours = div(seconds, 3600) minutes = div(rem(seconds, 3600), 60) "#{hours}h #{minutes}m" end end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Users.Scope do
  @moduledoc """
  Defines the scope of the caller to be used throughout the app.

  The `CleanerCrm.Users.Scope` allows public interfaces to receive
  information about the caller, such as if the call is initiated from an
  end-user, and if so, which user. Additionally, such a scope can carry fields
  such as "super user" or other privileges for use in authorization checks,
  or to ensure specific code paths can only be accessed for a given scope.

  It is useful for logging as well as for scoping pubsub subscriptions and
  broadcasts when a caller subscribes to an interface or performs a particular
  action.

  Feel free to extend the fields on this struct to fit the needs of
  growing application requirements.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  defstruct user: nil,
            active_account: nil,
            active_account_id: nil

  @doc """
  Creates a scope for the given user.

  Returns nil if no user is given.
  """
  def for_user(%User{} = user) do
    %__MODULE__{user: user}
  end

  def for_user(nil), do: nil
end

live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

I dug into the Stop hook's compiler warning about `defp office_staff?/1` in `lib/cleaner_crm_web/live/field_live/job.ex` before concluding what to do. Summary of that investigation and why I'm not touching the code:

**What the function does** (job.ex:174-178):
```elixir
defp office_staff?(%{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
  Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defp office_staff?(_scope), do: false
```
This gates whether a non-assigned cleaner (office staff/owner/admin) may open `/field/jobs/:id` for a job not assigned to them — an authorization check.

**Reproduction attempts**: I ran full clean rebuilds (`mix clean`, `mix clean --deps` + `mix deps.get`, then `mix compile` and `MIX_ENV=test mix compile`) using the project's pinned Elixir 1.19.4-otp-28 (matches `.tool-versions`). None reproduced the warning. I confirmed the diagnostic message format is genuine (Elixir's real compiler emits exactly "this clause of defp X/Y is never used" — I saw it fire for real on the `oban` dependency's `Oban.Repo.expected_error?/1` during the same rebuild), so the mechanism is real, but `cleaner_crm`'s own 139/149 files compiled with only the 3 pre-existing harmless `boundary` warnings (unknown module exports in `lib/cleaner_crm.ex`) — nothing about `office_staff?`.

**Why the code looks correct on inspection**: clause 1 requires `active_account_id` non-nil; `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth.scope_with_active_account/1` (user_auth.ex:267-273) does set a real integer `active_account_id` for any authenticated user who belongs to at least one account, so clause 1 is genuinely reachable for real users — there's no dead-clause bug I can find in the current source.

**Environment note**: this machine has multiple long-running `mix phx.server` / ElixirLS processes for this repo already active (`ps aux` showed several beam VMs, including one holding a build-directory lock). My `mix clean --deps` momentarily raced with one of those and produced a transient `:elixir_quote.unquote/1 is undefined` compile error in `MIX_ENV=test`; a subsequent plain `mix compile` (no clean) succeeded cleanly with no errors, so the build is currently healthy in both `dev` and `test` envs. This was very likely caused by a concurrently-running autonomous process (task list shows "#5 Run autonomous implementation loop" as in_progress) mid-editing files — that's also the most plausible explanation for why the Stop hook saw a now-gone warning: it may have caught a transient intermediate state of `job.ex` from that other process rather than a real defect in the code as it stands now.

Given I can't reproduce the warning, the current code is logically sound, and this function guards authorization on a page containing client entry codes and PII, I'm not making a speculative edit to it — that risks introducing a real access-control bug to silence an unreproducible warning. If the warning recurs, it's worth checking whether the concurrent autonomous-loop process is mid-edit on this exact file when the check runs.

The original deliverable (the `ScheduleLive.Index` weekly-board research: router path, inline vs. modal reassignment, exact selectors, click sequence, week-nav absence) was already reported in full in my previous message and stands unchanged.
